Bonnie Tyler's mural has been unveiled at Skewen Memorial Park in Neath Port Talbot

A mural of Bonnie Tyler has been unveiled in her hometown as a tribute to the global star "who never forgot her roots".

The Holding Out For a Hero singer, whose real name was Gaynor Hopkins, died in a hospital in Portugal in July , aged 75, after undergoing emergency intestinal surgery earlier this year.

Hundreds lined the streets of Skewen , in Neath Port Talbot, where she was born and raised, to pay their respects on the day of her funeral.

Artist Steve Jenkins, who painted the piece at Skewen Memorial Park, said it was "important" and the "pressure was on" to get the artwork right for the community.

Artist Steve Jenkins painted the "important" piece

The mural features a large picture of Tyler's face, as well as references to the local rugby club and Total Eclipse of the Heart - one of her best-known hits.

Speaking to BBC Wales, walkers passing the mural described the tribute as "fantastic".

Susan Petrosillo, 61, from Skewen, said she was "very, very proud".

"It's absolutely fantastic what they've done. It's such a lovely park as well," she said.

"She was such a big part of Skewen and still is."

Susan Petrosillo says it was "amazing" seeing everyone come together for Bonnie Tyler's funeral

On 17 August, a celebration of life service was held at Swansea Minster ahead of a private family funeral in the village.

Petrosillo added: "On the day of her funeral, the hearse came through Skewen and the amount of people who came out for that was amazing."

Michael Davies went to school with Bonnie Tyler and knew her "quite well"

For those who grew up alongside her, like Michael Davies, the mural is a chance to remember someone they knew long before she became a global superstar.

"I was in school with her, so I did know her quite well," he said.

"She was a Skewen girl, so it's tremendous."

Bob Marney said the rugby club emblem in the corner of the painting was important, as that's where Tyler performed her first audition

Bob Marney, 84, said the reference to the local rugby club - an emblem in the corner of the painting - was particularly significant.

"The rugby club is where she had her first audition," he said.

"She's a legend. She was down to earth, never forgot her roots. She never forgot Skewen."

The artist says the colourful side of Tyler's face represents how her music will live on, while the black-and-white side reflects the artwork's role as a memorial

For artist Jenkins, capturing Tyler's likeness came with "huge responsibility".

"I knew that I had to get it really accurate because of the emotions tied with Bonnie," he said.

"I knew that the family and the whole community were going to get quite emotional about seeing this, so it was important. The pressure was on."

Artist Steve Jenkins says the mural design evolved several times before reaching its final form

Jenkins, known as Jenks Art, said the design evolved several times before reaching its final form.

"The first mock-up we had had Mumbles Lighthouse in the background," he said.

"But [with Tyler] being so proud of being from Skewen, we decided to put Skewen Park in the background."

He added the two-tone design of Tyler's face also carried a deeper meaning.

"As I was painting it, and as I was being approached by people, it became apparent that her music is going to live on.

"And that's sort of represented in the colour side of the face, and then, being a memorial piece, the black-and-white side of the face represents that."

AI is leading the way in BBC Sport's prediction league table, but this week Chris Sutton has more than one machine to worry about.

His guest opponent for this weekend's fixtures is a computer game: Football Manager 27, the latest edition of the long-running management simulation series, which is released on 10 November.

The FM27 game engine has played out this weekend's matches and you can see its results, including goalscorers, below.

Miles Jacobson, the studio director of Sports Interactive, the company behind Football Manager, also joined in.

Do you agree with their predictions? You can pick your own below.

The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page.

A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points.

Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competition.

One of the features in Football Manager 27 allows you to customise your manager's visual appearance, with wheelchair-using managers included for the first time

Among the new features in Football Manager 27 [FM27] is the expanded ability to tweak your manager's visual appearance, including an option that means wheelchair-using managers are represented in the game for the first time.

"It's something we are really proud of," Jacobson told BBC Sport. "Some might think it is only a small thing, but for wheelchair users it is an absolutely massive thing to be able to be represented in the game that they love.

"I am not a teary person, but I have to admit I had some tears in my eyes last weekend when I was watching some Instagram videos from our free trial of the game, of disabled people who just wanted to be seen, and represented.

"It seems really obvious to those of us who have been represented in games for years, but just giving people an opportunity to be represented, when they haven't been before, really does mean a lot to them. That has just been brilliant to see."

A more immersive world has been created for FM27, which includes a new training system called Tactical Effectiveness.

"It reflects what happens in real life when a new manager comes into a club and does something different - it takes players a while to get used to the new tactics," Jacobson said.

"So, when you are the manager coming into a club, you have to decide whether to spend more time training the players in a really complicated tactic - which is going to take them a long time to learn and which means less time training them on other things - or do you start off with the basics, and build from there?

"It's a little bit like what Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner talked about after their performance in their defeat against Brentford last week, when he said he had been nice to his players, but now they have to listen and do what he is saying.

"I expect he is spending a lot of this week doing tactical effectiveness training in the background, or focusing on one part of it, because there are multiple elements."

Chris Sutton and Miles Jacobson were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'.

Like all the promoted teams, Coventry are having a go in games.

It has worked too, because they have picked up a few wins so far - they have three in the Premier League, as many as sixth-place Brentford .

It has been a strange season for the Sky Blues so far, because their performances have been a bit up and down. They can look very open, but those wins are the reward for their brave approach.

I don't see them getting anything here, however, on Frank Lampard's return to his former club.

Everton are not a free-scoring side, but I think they will have a bit too much nous for Coventry .

Miles' prediction: Both of these teams are in good form and this is probably the game I wrestled the most with before deciding what to go for. Thierno Barry has been a revelation for Everton this season and they showed against Newcastle that they can win without Jack Grealish, while Jack Rudoni has started to shine for Coventry at just the right time.

It's going to be a cracker of a game but I've gone with Everton to win, firstly because their defence is so strong at the moment, and Coventry might find them harder to break down than they did Sunderland , but also because David Moyes' side are playing with a lot of confidence now. 2-1

Tottenham always seem to do well against Leeds - they have only lost one of their past 15 meetings in the Premier League, going back almost 25 years.

I am a little bit of a believer that some teams always do well, or badly, against certain opposition or on certain grounds.

I had the same as a player when I had bogey teams or stadiums, as well as lucky ones. For example, while I always used to score against Everton at Goodison Park, I always had a stinker at Highfield Road, Coventry 's old home, despite getting plenty of goals against them in home games for Blackburn.

So, I am definitely not going for Leeds to win this - but do I back Tottenham to win again and continue their good run?

Roberto de Zerbi's side have rocketed up the table on the back of three wins in a row, although they were helped out a lot by Jean-Philippe Mateta's red card in their victory over Crystal Palace last time out.

Tottenham are flying at the moment, and their confidence is up - we are seeing a bit of a Spurs swagger for the first time in a long while. So, while I don't think they will make it four wins in a row, I don't see them being beaten, either.

It's likely to be a very tight game. Leeds were a bit unlucky to lose to Bournemouth last week, but their lack of goals is becoming an issue.

Miles' prediction: Leeds had such a brilliant start to the season, while Spurs have turned the corner and they have got lots of players coming back to full fitness. I can't separate them. 1-1

Hull are scrapping for points and hanging on in there in a lot of games.

I get a lot of my predictions wrong for their games because I always go for them to lose, but I am not going to do anything different for them this week because of who they are playing.

Arsenal are just monsters, aren't they? They always seem to find a way and do enough to win games, even when they don't play well, and they will grind another result out here if they have to.

Miles' prediction: Hull have been so entertaining, and I just absolutely love watching them because they play with no fear whatsoever. At the start of the season you would have looked at this and thought Arsenal would hit them for four or five, but I think it will be much closer than that because you can never write off Ollie McBurnie.

I enjoy watching Arsenal too, by the way, in the same way that I enjoy watching chess. They are a beautiful team to watch tactically and it is just difficult for them when they attack at the moment because they have lost a lot of their width with Bukayo Saka out injured. They seem to be grinding out a lot of their results but I still enjoy watching them - I enjoy watching any team, for different reasons. One of the beautiful things about football is there is no one set way to play it.

Arsenal often go 1-0 up and shut up shop, but they will have to do a bit more than that here, because Hull will keep going at them. 2-1

What are Newcastle ? What type of team are they? I am not sure and that's why their manager, Matthias Jaissle, is getting a bit of stick from Magpies fans.

Nottingham Forest just cannot score - they have managed only six league goals in their first nine games, the lowest total in the Premier League.

People seem to be unsure whether Brighton are really in the title race or not, but they are certainly in the mix for second place if Arsenal are the team we all think are going to win it.

Miles' prediction: What a revelation Brighton have been. They are just beautiful to watch and, again, they play with no fear. What they are doing on and off the pitch is just fantastic, but then you could say the same about Brentford . This will be a brilliant game and I wish I could watch it live. 2-2

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage was not helped by Mateta's sending-off in their defeat by Tottenham and the Eagles striker will miss this game after they failed with their appeal to overturn the decision.

Liverpool have issues too, and they come into this game off the back of a lousy performance and result against Fenerbahce on Wednesday.

Liverpool won't change the way they play under Andoni Iraola, so they will try to be aggressive with their press but are likely to be left open again if Palace get past it.

I don't see that happening this time, though, mostly because Palace have been so poor.

Liverpool were leaky against Fenerbahce, but I am going for them to keep a clean sheet here and get a sneaky away win, with Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola getting their goals.

Miles' prediction: I have mates who work at Palace and I know they probably won't talk to me for a week after this prediction, but I am going with Liverpool here. Mateta's suspension is huge for the Eagles, and Ismaila Sarr is still out injured. 0-2

Bournemouth have turned into one of the Premier League's form teams.

I thought they would run out of steam against Leeds last week but I was wrong, and they have shown they have got a bit of depth in their squad.

I've been surprised by Ipswich too, and they were unlucky not to beat Hull last time out. The Tractor Boys have got a bit of spirit about them, which makes me think they will get something from this game.

Bournemouth are a front-foot team under Marco Rose, who is a very attack-minded manager, but Ipswich will have a go too. I can see them getting a point.

Miles' prediction: I have been really impressed by Ipswich in the past few weeks and Julio Enciso has been doing really well for them - but Bournemouth are absolutely flying. What a season they are having. 0-2

I keep hearing how Sunderland boss Regis le Bris is under pressure. Really? After finishing seventh and getting a promoted side into Europe last season, it seems crazy that his job is at risk now.

They are also conceding an average of almost two goals a game in the Premier League, compared to 2025-26 when only three teams had a better defensive record.

Add that to their problems scoring - Forest are the only team with fewer goals so far - and you can see why they are bottom of the table.

I am still not sure how to judge Chelsea yet - yes, they beat Manchester United last week, but everyone beats Manchester United - but I just don't see the Black Cats keeping them out.

Miles' prediction: Sunderland are struggling with having European football and while I think they will turn things around, it won't be this week. Chelsea 's start to the new season has not been ideal and Joao Pedro being out injured is a huge loss to them - but I am still backing them here. 1-2

There were great scenes at Old Trafford on Tuesday with Manchester United coming back from 2-0 down to beat Roma, who had to field their third-choice goalkeeper because of injuries.

The head of France's CGT labour union, Sophie Binet (C), said the wave of protests and strikes had reached a new level

More than 600,000 protesters have taken part in rallies and marches across France, according to France's interior ministry, with five unions joining a day of action demanding more money for wages and public services.

The left-wing CGT union put the number of people taking part in Thursday's mobilisation at 1.57 million and hailed the figure as "a level unmatched" since 2023, citing big protests in Paris, Marseille, Bordeaux and Lille.

As darkness fell in Paris, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he would convene a "social conference" with unions and employers next Monday.

The wave of protests began in September over poor conditions and resources at lycées (high schools), before spreading to universities, workers and a revived "yellow-vest" movement against high prices.

The unions had vowed to take the co-ordinated move against the government "to the next level", and CGT chief Sophie Binet had said their message was that "the only thing that will bring this mobilisation to a halt is responding to our demands".

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had earlier deployed 70,000 police, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence.

Some unrest was reported in several cities.

A car was set alight near the Gallieni bridge over the Rhône river in Lyon, as hundreds of activists from the radical left-wing "black bloc" clashed with police.

Clashes were also reported in the north-western city of Rennes, where the local prefect said a "hostile group of masked individuals" had gathered in front of the main union march. Tear gas was used to clear a square in the south-western city of Bordeaux and a teenager was hurt in a stabbing involving a student at a high-school blockade in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris.

But the trouble was not on the scale seen during the last big day of protests, on Saturday 17 October, when more than 2,000 stores were looted and historic buildings set on fire.

The provisional numbers reported on Thursday were higher than on 17 October, considered the biggest day of rallies until now when the interior ministry said 550,000 people had turned out and the unions counted 800,000.

Earlier on Thursday the leader of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, said she would be happy if the protests matched that earlier level.

A car was set alight during a protest in the centre of Lyon

A coalition of unions across the public and private sector had urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government. In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, or Smic , which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour.

Sophie Binet told reporters at the start of a march in central Paris that protesters had "just reached a new level in their mobilisation" and were demanding immediate answers.

An estimated 9.89% of civil servants were taking part in the strikes, according to government figures.

Disruption was reported in schools, hospitals and public transport, and the Eiffel Tower and some exhibition rooms at the Louvre museum in Paris had to close.

Workers were also asked to halt production at oil refineries and France was expected to import more electricity than it produced on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants.

Disruption was already reported at schools on Thursday morning

The head of the CFDT complained that it was not just the minimum wage that needed to increase. "We are asking for a net increase of €100 a month," Marylise Léon explained.

The government has sought to appease public anger over rising prices, bringing down the cost of fuel by releasing 10 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves. Ministers have also promised school students to reform the unpopular Parcoursup university admissions platform and eventually replace it by 2028.

The prime minister said early on Thursday evening that Monday's "social conference" with unions and employers would seek to "provide answers to questions surrounding purchasing power and wages".

However, the government by its own admission has little room to manoeuvre, as it looks to make tens of billions of euros in savings, in a bid to cut the budget deficit to 5% of GDP.

The education ministry said that 16% of teachers had gone on strike on Thursday, and the unions said disruption had affected more than one in four lycées, which cater for 15-18 year-olds, as well as the vast majority of universities.

"Now it's not only about [investing in] public services in education and higher education, it's about all of the public services in France," the vice-president of the Unef student union, Alice De Brito, told the BBC.

Meanwhile, a revived gilets jaunes (yellow-vest) movement that staged a revolt against the high cost of living several years ago has called for further blockades and protests on Friday and Saturday too.

France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police

Thursday's march was eventually allowed in central Paris, although not along the route proposed by the unions between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Concorde, which would have taken protesters near the National Assembly, the Élysée Palace, and the prime minister's residence at Hôtel Matignon.

Instead, the march followed another central route from Place de la République to Place de la Nation.

The interior minister had earlier spoken of three potential risks on Thursday, from radical left "black blocs" groups and looting to wildcat marches without union authorisation.

Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has announced his resignation following a political crisis sparked by the collapse of a bank linked to him.

"I want to apologise to the people if at any point I failed," he said in a video message on social media. "It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me."

The crisis erupted after Ueno Bank entered an insolvency process, which froze all operations. Lawmakers accused Peña, who was a shareholder until last year in the company that owned the bank, of conflicts of interest and misconduct.

Peña rejected suggestions of impropriety. His resignation came as Paraguay's lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial.

Photos taken near Paraguay's Congress building on Thursday show police officers clashing with protesters demanding Peña be removed from office.

Paraguay's congress must approve the resignation of a president. But a special session convened on Thursday to address his resignation was adjourned in favour of continuing with the impeachment process.

Congress has scheduled a special session for Friday, when Peña is expected to present his defence, according to Reuters news agency.

In a post on X, Peña confirmed he would appear for Senate impeachment proceedings, adding that he would do so to "exercise my right to a defence".

He wrote: "I will provide the information requested of me. Citizens deserve to know the truth, without cover-ups and without anyone being above the law."

Peña earlier said his resignation was to protect stability, social peace and democratic institutions.

Ueno Bank has said it has about three million customers, equivalent to about 60% of Paraguay's adult population.

It held pensions and some other public funds and, after its collapse earlier this week, millions could not access their accounts.

The central bank seized the digital lender, and people took to the streets protesting and demanding Peña's resignation.

A new president of the Central Bank of Paraguay has been appointed and Congress has approved a process to pay depositors.

Protesters gathered near the Paraguayan Congress on Thursday

Peña won election in 2023 representing Paraguay's ruling conservative Colorado Party, beating a centre-left challenger.

The Colorado party dropped impeachment proceedings against Vice President Pedro Alliana, who is next in line for the presidency after Peña.

The Aer Lingus plane at Evreux military air base in France after being diverted following a bomb threat

At least 21 aircraft and several airports across Europe have been targeted by bomb threats in the second such incident this week, with the UK calling it a "malicious hoax".

Flights to Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, France, Italy, Poland and Romania were affected. An Aer Lingus plane from Dublin to Rome was diverted to an air base in France and Italian fighter jets escorted Finnair's Helsinki-Rome flight.

EasyJet said its flights from Newcastle and Glasgow were met by police in Prague as a precaution. London Heathrow and Birmingham airports received threats that were assessed as not credible.

No explosives have been found during searches, and it is not clear if the incidents, some claimed by a little known group, are related.

Who could be behind hoax bomb threats to European air travel?

The airport authorities in Italy's capital Rome said the hoax threat against two inbound flights received on Thursday had come by email.

The warnings were signed on behalf of a group or individual calling themselves "Fighters of the Male State", claiming to be targeting a "feminist regime" and wanting to "make our mark on history".

They threatened to "turn the skies red" with explosions.

These details were first reported by Italian media and then confirmed to the BBC by Aeroporti di Roma, which manages both of the city airports.

"Fighters of the Male State" likely refers to the Russian group "Muzhskoi Legion" ( "Male Legion") - an ultra-right group with such extreme views it was banned by a Moscow court in 2021. Yet it retained tens of thousands of online followers as it cheered on the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in the following year.

But that email, even if genuine, is unlikely to provide the leads that police and airport authorities need to pin down who is generating these hoaxes and why.

UK transport secretary says flights hit by 'hoax threats'

UK Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander described Thursday's incidents as "malicious hoax threats."

She said the government was taking "these threats seriously", stressing that there were "established processes for dealing with hoax and malicious threats".

A UK government spokesperson later said the threats reported "in the early hours" of the day had been "resolved", without giving any further details.

Heathrow later said in a statement it had received a threat earlier in the day which was "deemed not credible", adding there was "no risk to passengers, colleagues or the aircraft".

"There are robust UK aviation security standards in place to assess and safely manage these types of situations," the statement said.

Meanwhile, a Birmingham Airport spokesperson told the BBC it had received a threat, after which "processes were immediately initiated in conjunction with emergency services and partners".

The following flights were targeted by threats on Thursday:

Aer Lingus said its flight from Dublin to Rome diverted to Normandy, landing safely. The company added that it was working to "re-accommodate customers to their final destination as soon as possible".

Two Finnair flights from Helsinki landed at their destinations as normal, the airline said. One was escorted into Rome's Fiumicino airport by Italian Air Force fighter jets, Aeroporti di Roma told the BBC, while the other landed in Vienna, Austria

Wizz Air said two flights which departed Milan were affected - one was heading to Warsaw, before being diverting to Vienna; the other landed safely in Bucharest, with teams inspecting the aircraft

Polish airline LOT said its flight from Warsaw to Brussels landed as planned, and "no suspicious items were found". Another LOT flight from Warsaw to Paris was stopped before take-off and the plane and baggage underwent a security screening, with no hazardous items found

Three Ryanair flights landed in Bulgaria, according to Bulgarian media - one from Copenhagen and another from Madrid landed in the capital Sofia, while a third coming from London bound for Sofia landed in Plovdiv. The flights were escorted by Bulgarian air force fighter jets

No explosives were found on four flights which landed in Prague, Czech police said. EasyJet later said its flights from Newcastle and Glasgow were among those affected. "Passengers on both flights disembarked normally," the company said

Aegean Airlines said it "was informed of a bomb threat" concerning two of its flights from Thessaloniki in Greece to Milan, and also from Athens to Vienna. It said threat was "unfounded", and both flights departed from the respective airports"

A Ryanair flight from Porto in Portugal landed safely in Milan as planned, with bomb disposal experts checking them on arrival, Italy's Ansa news agency reported

Spain's airport authority said it had received bomb threats affecting three flights at Madrid airport, but any threat was ruled out following inspections. Iberia later said two of its flights - Milan-Madrid and Rome-Madrid - were affected. It was not clear whether the third plane was the above reported Ryanair Madrid to Sofia flight

Air Serbia said its flight from Belgrade to Bucharest "landed safely at its destination airport", and after checks, a reported bomb threat was "assessed as unfounded"

Emily Noble, who was aboard the diverted Aer Lingus plane from Dublin to Rome, said she was about an hour into her flight to attend a friend's wedding in the Italian capital when passengers were told about a "technical" problem.

Later, as the Aer Lingus plane began circling for an unplanned landing in France, the pilot said there was a "security" issue, the 26-year-old from Dublin told BBC Verify.

On board it was "an odd experience," Noble said. "It was worrying because we didn't know what was going on, but we were all trying to be as calm as we could."

Noble says she could hear fighter jets during the landing and saw one touch down behind the aircraft.

After landing at the Évreux-Fauville air base in Normandy, passengers learned the flight had been the subject of a bomb threat.

Emily Noble, a passenger on a diverted Aer Lingus flight, told the BBC she was now waiting for transfer to Rome at an air base in France

Noble said they remained on board for two-and-a-half hours while police and military personnel carried out checks, including searches with sniffer dogs.

The passengers were later told they would be taken to an airport in Paris and another plane would fly them on to Rome.

Philip Baum, professor of aviation security at the University of Coventry, said the industry "faces multiple bomb threats every single day" but he had been "surprised" by this week's incidents.

A flight is diverted "only when the threat is credible and the authorities believe there is a potential of explosive device on board", he said.

He said the concern was that "if you issue enough hoax threats, then complacency could set in and a real threat could be ignored - or they could be a diversion".

Marco Chan, an aviation expert at Kingston University, told the BBC the threats were "most likely a hoax, but the system is right to treat it as real".

He said they were being viewed by some experts as "possibly part of a pattern of cheap, deniable disruption" to air travel.

Hoaxes can also come from copycats, he said, but "three days of incidents is too small a sample to separate coordination from contagion".

Two days ago, seven European flights, including two from the UK, were searched after bomb threats were made. No explosives were found on any of the planes after searches.

On Monday, a Wizz Air flight travelling from London Luton Airport to Sofia was escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet to Budapest after a mid-air bomb threat.

Could your phone history one day help you borrow Rwf100 million? Equity Bank Rwanda Managing Director Hannington Namara told journalists on Thursday evening that it is the direction the bank wants to take with EMMA, Equity’s mobile money app for Africa.

Namara made the remarks during EMMA’s launch, a major and historic milestone in Rwanda’s payments ecosystem. He said Rwandans may soon be able to borrow up to Rwf100 million through the app, with their data used as collateral.

He did not give a launch date for the borrowing feature or explain what data would count, how the bank would value it, or what protections users would have if they fell behind on repayments. For now, the Rwf100 million figure is a promise of what EMMA could offer, not a confirmed loan product available to customers.

The idea would move lending further from the traditional branch experience Namara described. “Gone are the days when you go to the branch and sit and they ask you, ‘Who’s your mother? Who’s your father?’” he said. With EMMA, people should be able to save, send and receive money, borrow and invest from home.

The prospect builds on Equity’s existing shift towards digital lending. In its 2024 integrated report, the bank said all its small and micro loans had been digitised, allowing customers to borrow by phone. The report also said Equity was using artificial intelligence to assist with credit decisions by drawing on multiple data sources. The bank reported more than 1.39 million customers in Rwanda at the end of 2024.

That makes Namara’s Rwf100 million projection both striking and consequential. Data-based lending could help people who lack conventional collateral or a long banking history access credit. But the promise raises practical questions: Which data will be used? How will customers consent to its use? How can errors be challenged? Will borrowers understand the cost and risks before accepting a loan?

Namara described EMMA as a service designed to expand beyond Rwanda into other African markets, but said educating users would be essential. He framed Equity’s ambition as moving beyond financial inclusion to “economic inclusion,” giving people the means to pursue their goals and build wealth.

“EMMA is not a word. It has a human face,” he said, inviting people to welcome the service into their homes. Whether it can deliver on that promise may depend on more than how much users can borrow. It will also depend on whether they can understand and trust the system making decisions about their money and data.

Very inspiring, Emma will largely help achieve the vision of social-economic prosperity of the people of Rwanda and Africa

Babivugiye mu Rukiko Rwisumbuye rwa Muhanga kuri uyu wa Kane tariki ya 05 Uguhsyingo, 2026.

Ubushinjacyaha bwavuze ko Nyabyenda Emmanuel yacukuye amabuye y’agaciro nta ruhushya afite, kuko Rugendabari Mining Company Ltd ahagarariye yambuwe ibyangombwa byo gukora ubucukuzi bw’amabuye y’agaciro hakaba hashize imyaka ibiri.

Ubushinjacyaha kandi buvuga ko Nyabyenda ashinjwa ibyaha 4 birimo: Gucuruza amabuye y’agaciro yacukuwe nta ruhushya, kwiba amabuye no kunyereza umusoro.

Abavoka bane bunganira Nyabyenda Emmanuel babwiye Urukiko ko mu gufata icyemezo kijuririrwa, ko habayeho kwirengagiza amategeko nkana, aho bavuze ko Nyabyenda afatwa nk’umuntu ku giti cye (Personne Physique) ucukura amabuye y’agaciro, kandi we ahagarariye Kampani ya Rugendabari Mining (Personne Morale).

Umwe yagize ati: “Itegeko rigenga ama Sosiyete mu Rwanda, ritanga umucyo ku ikurikiranwa ry’aba bombi mu ngingo zaryo za 24 na 92.”

Bavuze ko hiyongeraho itegeko ryihariye ryerekana ubucukuzi bw’amabuye y’agaciro mu Rwanda mu ngingo yaryo ya 63, na ryo ritanga ibihano kuri aba bombi, kuko uwacukuye amabuye ku giti cye afite ibihano, naho iyo ubwo bucukuzi bwakozwe na Sosiyete na yo icibwa amande.

Abunganira Nyabyenda beretse Urukiko ko uruhushya rwa Rugendabari Mining rukiriho kuko hari ibimenyetso RMB yitangiye ubwayo.

Ubushinjacyaha buvuga ko ibyo Abunganira Nyabyenda bagaragariza Urukiko nta shingiro bifite, kuko ibaruwa yo kuri 27/06/2024 yerekana ko yambuwe uruhushya, ikomeza gucukura amabuye y’agaciro mu buryo bunyuranyije n’amategeko.

Abavoka bavuga ko iyo baruwa Ubushinjacyaha bushingiraho, yandikiwe undi munyamigabane isubiza ubusabe bwe bwo kuwa Gatandatu taliki 06/05/2024, bwo kubatandukanya na SEAVEMC bari bahuriyeho muri Rugendabari Mining Company Ltd.

Bavuze ko nta baruwa n’imwe RMB yigeze yandikira Rugendabari Mining nka Sosiyete bakoranye amasezerano.

Ubushinjacyaha bwasabye Nyabyenda kugaragaza aho yishyuriye umusoro.

Basubiza ko nta nyandiko RRA yagaragaje yerekana ko hari umusoro iyi Kampani yanyereje.

Mu iburanisha kandi Ubushinjacyaha buvuga ko abakozi ba RMB ku rwego rw’Akarere, ndetse no ku cyicaro gikuru cy’iki kigo, basuye Kampani yitwa SEAVMC, abunganira Nyabyenda bakavuga ko nta SEAVMC iba muri aka Karere kuko hari ubuhamya bwatanzwe n’abayobozi ba RMB aho bavuze ko nta CEAVMC iba mu Karere ka Muhanga.

Abunganizi bakavuga ko no mu ikoranabuhanga (Database) ryerekana ko Rugendabari Mining Company Ltd ikora.

Interest rates have risen for the first time in more than three years and the Bank of England has signalled a further increase is likely unless the US-Iran war is resolved.

Rates rose to 4% from 3.75% in a bid to curb inflation mainly driven by the conflict's impact on global oil prices.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank's governor, said the decision "shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes", but warned "unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase".

The higher level will increase the cost of borrowing for things such as mortgages, loans and credit cards, but will also lead to higher returns on savings.

The Bank's rate-setting committee all backed increasing interest rates, with eight out of nine voting in favour of the rise to 4%. One member wanted an even bigger increase to 4.25%.

Bailey said the hike was warranted due to higher energy prices and pointed to what happens in the Middle East as the main factor in future decisions.

"Put simply, it requires real progress towards settling the conflict in the Middle East," the governor said.

Bailey said he could "see the argument" for a further rate hike, before taking a "more conditional approach" dependent on the path of energy prices and inflation in the coming months.

However, the views of members on the rate-setting committee differed on the path forward.

Clare Lombardelli agreed there was "likely to be a case for a further increase in rates in the near term", while Megan Greene went further, suggesting "additional hikes" might be likely depending on how inflation impacted wages, prices and the jobs market.

However, Alan Taylor said the rate rise was a "a risk-management 'one-for-now' insurance hike".

Inflation, which measures the pace of price rises over time, is well below its peak of a few years ago but remains above the Bank of England's 2% target and is expected to increase further next year.

Prices rose 3.5% in the year to September 2026 , largely due to higher fuel prices. Millions of households are also set to be hit by energy bill increases in January.

Higher fuel prices can lead to prices rising for a host of goods and staples as businesses pass on higher costs to customers.

But the Bank said there was "limited evidence" this had happened so far for goods, such as food, with some firms absorbing cost increases and accepting lower margins.

In an interview with the BBC, Bailey defended the decision to raise rates despite the Bank's assessment that inflation was yet to spread to other parts of the economy.

He said further increases in energy prices are putting upward pressure on inflation and "that's what we have to seek to lean against".

Patrick Bryson, from Brighton, is set to see his five-year mortgage term with a 3.51% interest rate end soon.

The best deal the 51-year-old can find is a 5.17% loan with HSBC, which means his repayments will jump from £1,420 to £1,680 a month from February.

"The only thing that bugs me about the mortgage is that after five years of paying it off we are now paying more than we were before," said the father-of-three. "That's a bit of a slap in the face."

The guitar teacher, who has a combined income of around £68,000 a year with his wife, who manages a care home, said the couple is feeling pressure on their finances and so have changed their shopping habits and are looking to reduce their subcription outgoings.

"Over the last year I have stopped buying wine, we don't go out to eat much anymore, we have knocked takeaways on the head. The prices are ridiculous," he said.

Three ways the interest rate rise could affect you

Faisal Islam: How high will interest rates go?

The Bank now expects inflation to peak at 4.9% in the middle of next year, higher than it originally estimated, and not return to 2% until 2028.

But in an "adverse scenario", where the US-Iran war could escalate further and send oil prices higher, inflation could reach 6.2% in 2027, it suggested.

While the UK cannot control global energy prices, the Bank raised rates, for the first time since August 2023, in order to limit the knock-on effects of high energy prices resulting in inflation going up across the board.

Its base rate is what it charges other banks and building societies to borrow money, which influences what customers for mortgages, loans, credit cards get charged, as well as savings rates.

The rate rise will see 510,000 tracker mortgage-holders see a £31 monthly jump in repayments, according to banking trade body UK Finance.

Homeowners on fixed deals will see no change, though future products may be affected.

However, people on variable deals will be impacted depending on how their lender reacts to the rate rise. Typically a 0.25pp rise means a £14 increase per month in repayments.

Muri iki gikorwa, abakoze Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi, bavuze ko bicuza kuba barijanditse muri iki cyaha ndengakamere bityo ko basaba imbabazi umuryango Nyarwanda, ndetse n’abarokotse Jenoside.

Gatera Asman umwe bagize uruhare muri Jenoside, yasabye imbabazi kuba yarijanditse mu cyaha ndengakamere.

Gatera ati “Nakoze icyaha cy’indengakamere, nsabye imbabazi umuryango wa Kambanda, n’Abanyarwanda bose, n’Imana yo mu ijuru namwe muteraniye aha mumbabarire. Nsinzwe urubanza imbere y’Imana n’abantu.”

Murorunkwere Clementine warokotse we n’abana batatu mu muryango we, avuga ko yahaye imbabazi Gatera Asman wagize uruhare mu rupfu rw’umuryango we.

Ati “Ku bw’iyi Leta dufite ubu ngubu, njye n’umuryango wanjye, twiyemeje kuguha imbabazi twivuye inyuma, nta buryarya, turashaka kubaka igihugu cyacu.”

Undi na we wasabye imbabazi ati “Muri Jenoside nakoze icyaha cy’indengakamere […] by’umwihariko nkaba nsaba umuryango wa Butsure imbabazi, nkasaba n’igihugu imbabazi, n’umuryango w’Abacitse ku icumu rya Jenoside, Imana muri rusange, iteraniro ryose, mutubabarire ntabwo tuzongera gukora icyaha ukundi.”

Umushumba Mukuru wungirije w’Itorero rya ADEPR mu Rwanda, Rev. Pasiteri Eugène Rutagarama, yavuze ko iki gikorwa kigamije gukomeza gusigasira ubumwe bw’Abanyarwanda.

Ati “Nk’Abanyarwanda tubifite mu nshingano ko tugomba kubaka, ndetse tukarinda ubumwe bw’Abanyarwanda. Ni inshingano duhabwa n’amategeko yacu. Tugomba kubikora ntabwo bireba ADPER gusa ,birandeba aho nsengera,mu buyobozi ayoboye,mu itorero.”

Akomeza ati “Nk’Abanyamadini n’Amatorero ni inshingano Imana yaduhaye, yabitubwiye binyuze mu ijambo ryayo ngo njye narangije kubiyungaho binyuze mu mwana wange, ariko aduha inshingano zo kunga n’abandi bene wacu, abo duturanye n’abo tubana.”

Umuyobozi w’Agateganyo w’Akarere ka Gatsibo, IBINGIRA Frank, yavuze ko gusaba imbabazi atari umuhango ahubwo bigomba kugaragarira mu bikorwa biteza imbere igihugu.

Ati “Buriya gusaba imbabazi no kuzitanga byabaye kandi ni byiza, ni intambwe ikomeye cyane ariko igikomeye kurusha ikindi kikazagira n’akamaro, ni ukubigaragaza mu mibanire isanzwe ya buri munsi, mu bikorwa bya buri munsi. Ku bakoze Jenoside basabye imbabazi ikindi leta ibategerejeho ni ukugira uruhare mu iterambere ry’igihugu, muri gahunda za leta kugira ngo na bo bateze imbere igihugu, dufatanye kubaka igihugu.”

Muri rusange abakoze Jenoside bakaza gufungurwa nyuma yo kurangiza ibihano 35 ni bo bemeye gusaba imbabazi abarokotse Jenoside muri 89 bari bahawe inyigisho z’ubumwe n’ubudaheranwa.

Egypt's Sondos Sonbol won gold in the women's wushu taolu changquan at Dakar 2026

After a spectacular opening ceremony which celebrated Senegalese national identity and wider African culture on Saturday, the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics are in full swing.

The continent's first ever Olympic event is showcasing new sports which have never appeared at any version of the Games before and has offered athletes predominantly aged 15 to 17 a place in the history books.

First-time Olympic medallists have been crowned in baseball5 and wushu taolu, while some of the rowers who secured places on the podium in coastal beach sprint events may well be eyeing up potential glory at the senior Los Angeles 2028 Games.

BBC Sport Africa examines what has attracted the most attention during the first week of competition.

Arguably the most eye-catching sport on show in Senegal has been this modern Chinese martial art, better known around the world as kung fu and practiced competitively in two forms via choreographed sequences or sparring.

Promoted by the government of the People's Republic of China to encourage friendly international exchange, the International Wushu Federation was established in 1990 to formalise centuries-old disciplines popularised by the likes of movie stars Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan and Michelle Yeoh.

Wushu has featured as an exhibition event or part of the cultural programme at past Games, but medals in changquan and tajiquan were up for grabs on its official debut as an Olympic sport.

Changquan combines speed, kicks, jumps and acrobatics while taijiquan is akin to tai chi and involves controlled movements which flow together in a precise performance set to music.

Morocco's Oussama El Maghnaoui missed out on a place in the final of the men's tajiquan

National team uniforms were dispensed with to allow competitors to wear their own flowing robes, which were often brightly coloured and enhanced with detailed designs.

"Everybody has a different kind of flavour to their moves," the United States' Marshall Brayton said.

"I think that uniqueness in every person's routine is the essence of wushu."

As jumps, flips and flourishes with weaponry caught the eye in changquan, setting moves to music came with its own challenges in tajiquan.

"I was advised to sleep to the song (used in performance)," eventual champion Zhe Nin Ng of Singapore said after day two of competition.

"I had to understand it more and have it in my muscle memory. I keep playing it again and again until I fall asleep."

All you need to know about the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics

Speed is the order of the day at the start and end of rowing's coastal beach sprint event, but in between competitors must also battle the waves

While rowing has been an Olympic staple since 1900, a new twist has been added with the arrival of this discipline on Senegal's Atlantic coast.

The competition begins on dry land with an athlete running down the beach, boarding their boat and rowing out 250m to a marker buoy before turning sharply and racing back.

Once they return to shore, they then jump out of the boat and sprint back up the beach to touch a buzzer on the finish line. The fastest time wins.

"It's super fun. It's a lot more exciting than traditional rowing," 17-year-old USA's Isaac Moos told Olympics.com.

Beachfront spectators have the benefit of being able to witness a whole race and the unpredictability of sea conditions adds an extra element to competition.

"The waves are constantly changing and one small mistake can cost you," said Su Juntao, who won gold for China in the mixed double sculls.

"You have to push for more speed while keeping your mistakes to a minimum. That's what makes it so challenging and exciting."

And this is just the start for coastal rowing at the Olympics, because it is set to replace the lightweight double sculls category at LA 2028.

Host nation Senegal finished eighth in the baseball5 competition, with Cuba taking gold after beating Chinese Taipei in the final

Baseball will also be included on the schedule in California in four years' time, but an urban, simplified version of the sport kicked off the action in Dakar last Friday.

Introduced to increase accessibility and taking inspiration from street games, the five-a-side version does not require equipment and featured mixed-gender teams on its Olympic debut.

With no pitcher, players for the 'batting' side using their hand to hit the rubber ball from a standing position on an 18m x 18m court featuring four bases.

There are no strikes, meaning each 'batter' gets just one chance to hit the ball legally as they attempt to score as many runs as possible before their team suffers three outs.

Played over five innings, it is faster-paced than its bigger brother and skills are rewarded over strength.

Cuba, the nation at the top of the all-time Olympic baseball medal table with three golds, fittingly opened the competition with a victory over Turkey.

"We have baseball running through our veins and in our hearts, and we will always, always, always put Cuba at the top," player Jean Carlos Machado Casado told Olympics.com.

South Africa's Molemo Losaba failed to reach the final of the men's street skateboarding

While Olympics fans are used to seeing beach volleyball, two more traditional sports have been given a twist in Senegal.

Handball and wresting events have also been relocated to Saly's beach, known for its fine sand and turquoise waters.

Featured in continental and world championships, and promotional events organised by governing body United World Wrestling, beach wrestling fittingly makes its Youth Olympics debut in Senegal, where traditional forms of wrestling remain incredibly popular.

Two athletes contest bouts inside a circular area on sand, scoring points through throws, takedowns, or forcing the opponent out of bounds.

Matches, to be contested this weekend, are expected to be short and fast-paced.

Eight-a-side handball, which also featured at the Buenos Aires Youth Games in 2018, will be among the final events contested at Dakar 2026.

Skateboarding, first included in the senior Olympic schedule at Tokyo 2020, also made its Youth Games debut in Dakar.
